rows.before: STRIDED_ENTRY_HEADER_LEN = 8 (mismatched the parser's headerLen=6, causing catalog and mail text writes to start 2 bytes too far into each 168-byte entry; the writer left 2 stale header bytes at +6..+7 and overshot the trailing 2 bytes of the 168-byte slot, so on reload the parser decoded the stale bytes as the leading UTF-16 codepoint of the entry — visually 'the edit didn't take')
rows.after: STRIDED_ENTRY_HEADER_LEN = 6 (matches the parser's header length; empirically the catalog entry at body 0x162B6 begins its UTF-16 text at +6 with the bytes 57 00 45 00 45 00 4B 00 4C 00 59 00 = 'WEEKLY' in tongari_en.dsv)
rows.reason: root cause of the announcement edit-save bug — writer offset was off by 2 bytes; catalog and mail edits now round-trip cleanly

rows.after: PendingEdit union now includes: ritch | player_name | school_name (NEW) | catalog | catalog_clear (NEW) | mail | garden_tile

rows.before: Wrote player name to one location only (body 0x1149C, 22-byte field) on both slot A and slot B
rows.after: Writes player name to THREE mirror copies on both slot A and slot B: (1) body 0x47E width 10 bytes (§22 canonical authoritative copy), (2) body 0x1149C width 22 bytes (character-record per-display copy, archive's existing parsed location), (3) body 0x114BA width 10 bytes (§12.1 secondary cached copy). Tightest mirror is 10 bytes — payload cap stays at 5 chars per §22.
rows.reason: save-load-screen title reads from the §22 location in some builds; mirroring ensures the edited name shows wherever the game reads from

rows.after: New 'school_name' edit kind. Writes school/town name to TWO mirror copies on both slot A and slot B: (1) body 0x114B2 width 12 bytes (empirically observed in v2.31 EN saves — 'Shop' lives here in tongari_en.dsv), (2) body 0x115B2 width 12 bytes (§5 documented offset; empty in v2.31 corpus but present-in-case-some-build-reads-from-it). Cap 6 chars / 12 bytes UTF-16 LE.
rows.reason: feature 2 of the brief — school name now editable

rows.after: New 'catalog_clear' edit kind. Zero-fills the entire 168-byte entry on both slots, then writes the empty-slot sentinel 0xFF 0xFF at +0xA6..+0xA7 to mimic the fresh-save empty-slot byte pattern (verified against entries 4..6 of tongari_en.dsv). Parser's plausible-text heuristic then skips the cleared slot so it disappears from the inspector list and the in-game catalog screen.
rows.reason: additional requirement — players can remove unwanted announcements, not just edit them

rows.before: schoolName: 0x47e, schoolNameLen: 12 (step-250 reclassification labeling body 0x47E as 'school name' based on save14's 'Revere' reading — a one-save inference that did not hold under wider testing)
rows.after: schoolName: 0x114b2, schoolNameLen: 12 (v2.31 EN saves consistently store the shop/school name at body 0x114B2; tongari_en.dsv has 'Shop' there). Also added playerNameCanonical: 0x47e, playerNameCanonicalLen: 10 — surfaced as a parallel read so users can see if their §22 copy has drifted from the character-record copy.
rows.reason: step-250 inferred school name was at 0x47E from a single save; the wider corpus shows 0x47E is the §22 player-name copy and the school name lives at 0x114B2. Inspector now reads the right slot.

rows.after: profile range: 'player body[0x47E] + body[0x1149C] + body[0x114BA]; school body[0x114B2] (+ §5 mirror body[0x115B2])'; catalog range: 'body[0x162B6+], 168-byte stride (6-byte header + 162-byte UTF-16 text body)'

rows.after: Profile section now exposes an inline-edit affordance for BOTH player name (cap 5 chars per §22) and school name (cap 6 chars per §5). If the §22 canonical copy has drifted from the character-record primary, a 'stale — will be overwritten on next edit' note appears next to the display value.
rows.reason: feature 2 + 3 of the brief — school name and player name now editable from the UI

rows.before: Catalog entry rows had only an 'Edit catalog text' inline affordance. No way to remove an announcement.
rows.after: Catalog entry rows now have an 'Edit catalog text' affordance AND a 'Remove announcement' button. Staging a remove drops any pending text edit for the same slot (and vice versa). Removed slots render strike-through with a 'staged for removal' tag in the live preview; downloaded .sav has those slots zero-filled with the FF FF empty-slot sentinel so the in-game catalog screen treats them as empty.
